name: Chana Masala
description: Pakistani chana masala with tender chickpeas simmered in a tangy onion-tomato masala with ginger, green chillies and warm spices.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked chickpeas, tender and drained with some cooking liquid reserved
Salt to taste and fresh coriander for finishing
method: Heat the oil in a pot, add the cumin seeds and let them become aromatic, then add the onions and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, followed by the tomatoes, green chillies, coriander powder, red chilli, turmeric and salt.
Cook the masala until the tomatoes have broken down and the mixture looks cohesive, stirring often so the spices do not catch on the base.
Add the already tender chickpeas with a little reserved cooking liquid and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so they absorb the masala flavour.
Mash a small portion of the chickpeas against the side of the pot and stir them back into the gravy for natural body without turning the whole dish into a paste.
Adjust the gravy with a little more chickpea liquid if needed, then finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.
Taste for salt and chilli and serve hot with roti, naan or rice.
image_alt: Pakistani chana masala with tender chickpeas in thick onion tomato masala, green chilli and coriander
image_caption: Tender chickpeas simmered in a cooked onion-tomato masala and lightly mashed for natural gravy body.
technique: The chickpeas must already be tender before they meet the masala. Build a thick onion-tomato base first, then simmer the cooked chickpeas in it and mash only a small portion for body so the final dish still contains whole chickpeas.
doneness_cues: Chickpeas should mash easily with a fork and have no hard centre.
Tomato masala should look cohesive rather than watery before chickpeas are added.
Gravy should cling to the beans after simmering.
Only a small percentage of chickpeas should be mashed for thickening.
mistakes: Using undercooked chickpeas and expecting the masala simmer to tenderise them quickly.
Adding too much reserved cooking liquid at once.
Mashing most of the chickpeas and losing the intended texture.
Adding garam masala early enough that its aroma disappears.
substitutions: Canned chickpeas work if rinsed and drained thoroughly.
Reserved chickpea cooking liquid gives better continuity than plain water but use it gradually.
Green chilli can be reduced while keeping cumin and coriander for aroma.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered. The gravy thickens as chickpeas continue absorbing liquid.
reheating: Reheat gently with a small splash of hot water if the gravy has become too thick.
serving: Serve with roti, naan or rice and fresh coriander.

faqs.question: Why is chana masala watery?
faqs.answer: The masala may not have reduced before chickpeas were added, or too much cooking liquid was used. Simmer uncovered and mash a small portion of beans.

faqs.question: Why are my chickpeas hard?
faqs.answer: They were not fully tender before the masala stage. Cook dried chickpeas completely first.

faqs.question: Can I use canned chickpeas?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rinse and drain them well, then simmer in the finished masala long enough to absorb flavour.
